question: Does small-scale SiLU lose target-aligned even features rather than merely scale all gradients?

predictions.claim: RMS-normalized ReLU features and learning curves are invariant to positive weight scale.
predictions.criterion: paired maximum training/test-MSE curve difference below 1e-8 across scales
predictions.scope: all controls except finite-epsilon LayerNorm tolerance 1e-4

predictions.claim: For no-LN SiLU, even-feature/odd-feature squared-energy ratio grows approximately as scale squared in the two smallest scales.
predictions.criterion: median ratio at scale0.2 divided by ratio at scale0.05 lies between 10 and 20; expected factor16

predictions.claim: At scale0.05 without LN, SiLU quadratic-target initial progress is below one tenth ReLU despite equal total feature RMS; the linear-target initial progress is not below one half ReLU.
predictions.criterion: target-aligned kernel-energy ratios and measured first-step MSE reductions satisfy both bounds in median across seeds

predictions.claim: Preactivation LN removes most input weight-scale dependence and linear skip fails to restore the weak quadratic SiLU channel.
predictions.criterion: LN target-aligned energy changes below1% between0.05 and1; linear_skip at0.05 does not double quadratic energy relative to none
predictions.scope: fixed width64, Gaussian symmetric dataset, frozen hidden

predictions.claim: The fixed-feature gradient-descent spectral recurrence predicts measured train curves.
predictions.scope: all216 seed conditions; this checks execution and a scoped model, not novel universal theory

analysis.research_units: two target functions and exact recipes; six seeds are within-condition repeats
analysis.endpoint: finite results are retained regardless of benchmark cutoff
analysis.source: analytic parity decomposition plus new synthetic data; frozen KB is development motivation
